subject: Careers
title: Following instructions and teamwork
lesson_success_checks: Use written and spoken instructions in the paired assembly task. Try reader and maker roles with usual access. Review six features of a clear instruction. Record a clarification or check, self-assess five Week 1 expectations and choose a next step.
source_assessment_summary: Formative review; staff confirm any later accredited mapping from actual evidence.
accreditation: The qualification/accredited unit, mapping confirmed by staff; no named scheme or awarding body.
calendar_note: Year A. Spring 1 Week 4, 25–29 January 2027. Friday 29 January 2027, P1. One forty-minute formative lesson for a pair. Six-week term 4 January–12 February; Week 6 assessing. No clock time supplied.
timing: Recall one expectation and honest work record; agree access.
Model clear written/spoken steps, repeat meaning and check.
Rehearse roles, use the six-item checklist and private hinge.
Two six-minute rounds; reset and swap reader/maker roles.
Short clarity reflection, five self-ratings, one next step/reply and save.

source_timing.note: Minute phases and paired round guides authored, not prescribed by row 91.

source_adaptation: B91 Spr1·W4 and C91 exact outcome retained. Inherited framework/resource context from row 88 generic. Row 91 gives no minute sequence: authored 5/8/10/12/5 lesson. Same business/order/roles as Week 1; reader and maker enact the checker and preparer roles. Written and spoken instructions, shared meaning check, reset and role swap implement the owner brief. Two six-minute classroom rounds are guides, not a speed target. Supported/Standard/Stretch retained.

sources.note: Uploaded snapshot read directly; B91/C91 exact. Inherited identifying labels generic. Raw workbook not distributed; no current repository check claimed.
Accepted business continuity, editions/tier/cover structure and unchanged generic workroom bank; only controlled view D used in Week 4.
Business, order, roles, five expectation labels/meanings and four self-rating statements retained exactly. Reflection clue for finished work stays activity-neutral.

Friday 29 January P1, pair, forty minutes. Written and spoken paired assembly instructions: one reads and one does, then swap. Clear-instruction checklist, short when-I-did-not-understand reflection and Week 1 expectations self-review. No real employer, product or place. Weeks 5–6 one per return; pause for Downloaded.

routes.Supported: Use four numbered steps, a reader/maker role card, model and sentence starts. Hear one step, say or show its meaning, do it and check. Keep the written steps and usual aid. Adult partner or exact scribe valid. Try both roles and keep your own reflection and five ratings.
routes.Standard: Use written and spoken steps to make and check two paper packs, then reset and swap roles. Review the six clear-instruction checks and explain one judgement. Record what you did when a step was unclear, or a check that helped. Rate the five Week 1 expectations.
routes.Stretch: Explain why an instruction could be misunderstood and improve it without changing the order. Compare the planned roles with what happened and explain one teamwork adjustment. Check the result against the order; use the same reflection and five expectations. Extra writing optional.

business.description: An invented small business prepares simple paper packs for customers. It has a supervisor, a preparer and a checker. It has no name, real employer, location or contact details. This is classroom simulation only.
business.order: Prepare two paper packs. Each pack needs one large card and one paper strip. Put the items beside each other. Check both packs against this order. Tell the checker when they are ready.
business.roles: The preparer arranges the materials. The checker reads the order and checks each pack. Agree roles, then swap after resetting the materials. An adult can take the other role if preferred.
business.limits: Use ready-cut paper only. No scissors, staplers, machines, food, money, customer data, live orders or deliveries. Accuracy, communication and support matter; speed is not assessed.

task_header: Make two paper packs. Use two large cards and two paper strips. No tools are needed.

instructions.action: Place two large cards side by side.
Put one paper strip beside each card, not on top.
Check: each pack has one card and one strip.
Tell the reader what is ready or needs a check.

help_instruction: If a step is unclear, pause. Re-read or ask the reader or adult to explain the step. Check the meaning before doing it.

role_routine.reader: Read the order, then one numbered step aloud. Wait for the maker to say or show the meaning. Re-read or use the agreed help if needed.
role_routine.maker: Keep the written steps visible. Say or show what the step means, ask if unclear, then do the step. Use your usual aid.
role_routine.check: Together compare both packs with the written order. State any unfinished step honestly.
role_routine.swap: Reset the same materials and swap reader and maker for round two. Each learner has their own record. An adult can take the other role.

rounds.action: Agree roles. Reader reads, maker checks meaning and makes. Together check and record actual role.
Reset, swap reader and maker, repeat and check. Record each actual role and any help.

clear_model: Put one paper strip beside each large card.
reflection_alternatives: Nothing was unclear today; a check that helped was…
I did not try this part yet; the help I need is…

expectations.label: Readiness and reliability
expectations.meaning: Know the agreed start and task. Get agreed materials ready. Tell the supervisor if a delay or support need affects the plan.
expectations.look_for: I checked the task and materials or asked for help to get ready.

expectations.label: Respectful communication
expectations.meaning: Listen or read, use respectful words and check meaning. You can ask for a pause or private help.
expectations.look_for: I listened or read and used a clear question or reply.

expectations.label: Instructions and quality
expectations.meaning: Check the steps. Ask if unsure. Check the finished work against the order before saying it is ready.
expectations.look_for: I checked a step or the finished packs against the order.

expectations.label: Safety and help
expectations.meaning: Keep the work area and access clear. Use only agreed materials. Stop and tell the supervisor if something is unsafe or unclear.
expectations.look_for: I kept the area clear or asked before doing an unclear task.

expectations.label: Teamwork and responsibility
expectations.meaning: Agree roles, share information and report mistakes honestly. Ask for a workable adjustment when needed.
expectations.look_for: I agreed a role, shared a useful update or reported a mistake.

reflection_prompts: I checked the task and materials or asked for help to get ready.
I listened or read and used a clear question or reply.
I checked a step or finished work against the instruction.
I kept the area clear or asked before doing an unclear task.
I agreed a role, shared a useful update or reported a mistake.
rating_states: I did this with a prompt
worked_examples_status: All worked examples, workplace and model instructions are invented and declared. Record actual roles, meaning checks, result, help and reflection honestly. No real employer, person, product or place named.
private_help_route: Trusted adult or school help route. Point to HELP, write or ask privately. If one adult is busy, use the route to another. Pass, pause and supported return available. No personal employment, family or accident account requested.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Evidence Sheet pages 2–3: blank paired task/reflection log and five-expectation review. Page 1 includes six blank checklist judgements. Book/voice/aid/typing/exact scribe valid; read back/correct. Record actual roles and any unobserved parts.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: four numbered steps, one step at a time, checklist and reduced repetition. Communication and Interaction: rehearsal, wait time, visible order, usual aid and exact scribe/readback. SEMH: predictable roles, private review, pass and pause/return. Sensory and Physical: clear accessible table, seated roles and large print. EAL: plan in any language. 1 Point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 scaffold/choice; 5 model first step only then return task.
worked_example_and_fade: After the model ask what goes beside each large card and how many. Key: one paper strip beside each card, not on top. Keep header, steps, model and normal aids; fade answer cues only. Repeat meaning may be a word, selected phrase or demonstration. A usual reading/communication aid is access, not automatically a content prompt.

main_hinge.claim: Pause and ask for a clear meaning before acting on an unclear step.

parallel_hinge.claim: Compare the result with the written instruction rather than guess that it is finished.

assessment: Keep each learner’s actual reader/maker roles, a task/result check, six checklist judgements and one improvement, a short clarification or check reflection, five Week 1 self-ratings and one next step/reply. Ratings exactly: I did this; I did this with a prompt; I need another try; Not seen today. Normal access differs from supplying thinking. Judge observable instruction use, clarification and teamwork; no personality, reading-fluency or pace score.

evidence.description: Individual actual reader/maker record, six checklist judgements and one improvement, short clarity reflection, five expectation ratings, evidence clue and next step/reply.

where_this_leads: This helps me check what an instruction means, work with a partner and ask for useful clarification in learning or future work.
colour_blind_safe: Numbered steps, written labels and words carry meaning; no colour-only states.

asset.description: Unchanged generated workroom bank from accepted Week 3, originally Week 2. Only controlled view D used, in native crops; generic invented workers/workplace.

sequence_next.scope: Not authored. One per return after Downloaded. Further GROW Careers paused.

Careers · LAUNCH · a pair of learners · Spring 1 Week 4 · formative
Theme: Resilience & Change. Six-week term, 4 January–12 February; Week 6 assessing. Thread tags: SMSC So/M (S/C none); British Values MR/IL (D/RL/T none).
Source: LAUNCH Weekly - Spring row 91, B91 Spr1·W4 and C91 exact. Inherited framework/resource context from row 88 generic; no registration or award completion inferred.

Use written and spoken instructions in the paired assembly task. Try reader and maker roles with usual access. Review six features of a clear instruction. Record a clarification or check, self-assess five Week 1 expectations and choose a next step.

An invented small business prepares simple paper packs for customers. It has a supervisor, a preparer and a checker. It has no name, real employer, location or contact details. This is classroom simulation only.

Keep the Week 1 two-pack order. Reader is the checker role for this task; maker is the preparer. Adult is supervisor and can partner. Use the Week 2 keep-clear/report routine and Week 3 honest progress record. No real customer, employer, product or place.

Two large ready-cut cards and two paper strips per pair, plus spares; written steps, role routine, six-item checklist, tier pack, vocabulary, books or blank Type instead record and usual aids. Reset/reuse materials between rounds. Keep the written instructions visible; do not turn the task into a memory or listening test.
This helps me check what an instruction means, work with a partner and ask for useful clarification in learning or future work.
Recall one expectation and honest work record; agree access.
Model clear written/spoken steps, repeat meaning and check.
Rehearse roles, use the six-item checklist and private hinge.
Two six-minute rounds; reset and swap reader/maker roles.
Short clarity reflection, five self-ratings, one next step/reply and save.
5 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 5 = 40 minutes. Source row 91 gives no minute sequence; these phases are authored. Processing and brief pauses included. Times guide the routine; speed is not assessed.

0–5: retrieve a Week 1 expectation and Week 3 honest task-record idea; agree roles, access and private help. 5–9: compare the invented unclear instruction “Put stuff there quickly.” with “Put one paper strip beside each large card.” Explain what, how many and where. 9–13: adult models reading one written step aloud; maker says or shows its meaning, does it and checks. Check after model: one strip for each card, beside rather than on top. Keep model and written order visible.

13–19: rehearse reader/maker routine and the six checks: Goal, Parts, Order, Exact words, Finish check and Help. Apply them to the whole written task, including its header and help line. Record Clear, Needs a change or Not checked yet; accept justified concerns. Each learner chooses one improvement, rather than copying an adult answer. 19–23: private hinge B pause/ask if unclear instead of guessing. Parallel A compare work with the instruction rather than assume it is finished. Re-model and recheck privately.

23–29 round one: agree reader/maker, read the order and one step aloud, say/show meaning, assemble and compare both packs with the order. 29–35: reset the same paper, swap reader and maker and repeat/check. Each learner records actual roles and help. Pause or reduce repeated output for access, keeping the role swap as an offered opportunity. An adult can partner. Missing roles remain Not seen today; never claim the planned swap happened if it did not.

35–38: short individual reflection “When I didn't understand I…” Or use: Nothing was unclear today; a check that helped was… / I did not try this part yet; the help I need is… Rate the five Week 1 expectations using actual evidence. 38–40: privately check one evidence clue, set one NS, keep the reply and next review time; save each record. Pointing, voice or exact scribe is valid; no public performance or personal history requested.

Use four numbered steps, a reader/maker role card, model and sentence starts. Hear one step, say or show its meaning, do it and check. Keep the written steps and usual aid. Adult partner or exact scribe valid. Try both roles and keep your own reflection and five ratings.

Use written and spoken steps to make and check two paper packs, then reset and swap roles. Review the six clear-instruction checks and explain one judgement. Record what you did when a step was unclear, or a check that helped. Rate the five Week 1 expectations.

Explain why an instruction could be misunderstood and improve it without changing the order. Compare the planned roles with what happened and explain one teamwork adjustment. Check the result against the order; use the same reflection and five expectations. Extra writing optional.

After the model ask what goes beside each large card and how many. Key: one paper strip beside each card, not on top. Keep header, steps, model and normal aids; fade answer cues only. Repeat meaning may be a word, selected phrase or demonstration. A usual reading/communication aid is access, not automatically a content prompt.

One reads the written step aloud; the maker can also see the steps and use the normal aid. Reading support, agreed communication aid or adult voice can carry the learner’s selected message. Maker checks meaning before acting. Each has a turn in both roles through reset/swap, with adult partner if preferred. No blindfold, hidden instruction, racing or removal of aids.

Cognition and Learning: four numbered steps, one step at a time, checklist and reduced repetition. Communication and Interaction: rehearsal, wait time, visible order, usual aid and exact scribe/readback. SEMH: predictable roles, private review, pass and pause/return. Sensory and Physical: clear accessible table, seated roles and large print. EAL: plan in any language. 1 Point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 scaffold/choice; 5 model first step only then return task.

Trusted adult or school help route. Point to HELP, write or ask privately. If one adult is busy, use the route to another. Pass, pause and supported return available. No personal employment, family or accident account requested.

Evidence Sheet page 1 has the six clear-instruction checks with blank judgements. Page 2 is a blank typed paired-task record, including one instruction improvement and the short clarity reflection. Page 3 has five blank self-ratings/evidence clues and next step/help/reply. Page 4 is the private staff record. Book/usual aid default; all tiers use the same evidence goal.

Keep each learner’s actual reader/maker roles, a task/result check, six checklist judgements and one improvement, a short clarification or check reflection, five Week 1 self-ratings and one next step/reply. Ratings exactly: I did this; I did this with a prompt; I need another try; Not seen today. Normal access differs from supplying thinking. Judge observable instruction use, clarification and teamwork; no personality, reading-fluency or pace score.

VF, WS, I, NS, //, ?, E and R generic codes. E actual banked work. R after Voice, Audience, NS and reply in the same colour, on the same page or usual mode. One NS might make a question more exact or add a result check. Retain first try and reply. Offer to Communication portfolio; staff confirm any accredited mapping. A classroom simulation does not prove workplace competence or real placement attendance.

Ready-cut paper only. No tools, machines, money, food, live customers, personal data or deliveries. Keep the area clear. Stop/keep clear/report actual concerns and follow school procedures. Do not create hazards for the task. Listen calmly to concerns, avoid probing or secrecy promises and follow the usual school route; keep private concerns outside shared evidence.
